name: Cosam
overview: Cosam is a male figure noted in the genealogy of the Messiah as recorded in Luke 3:28. While no tribal affiliation or additional notes are provided, his inclusion in this lineage underscores his part in the ancestral line leading to Jesus Christ.
namesAndTitles: The name Cosam appears as a proper name in Scripture without a given meaning or divine origin. The biblical record simply identifies him by this name in the genealogy found in Luke 3:28.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Cosam as the son of Addi and the father of Elmadam, establishing a direct father-son lineage. These relationships are explicitly and implicitly noted in Luke 3:28, linking him within the ancestral line of Christ.
scriptureSignificance: Cosam's significance lies in his role within the Messianic genealogy, which traces the human ancestry of Jesus Christ. His presence in this lineage highlights the fulfillment of God's promise through a specific ancestral line, emphasizing the historical reality of Christ's human descent. Although details about his life are sparse, his mention affirms the continuity of God's redemptive plan through generations.
